Pune Startup Froncort.AI Gets $2.3 Mn Google.org Grant For AI Disease Screening App
Froncort.AI, a Pune-based healthcare AI startup, has received a $2.3 million grant from Google.org to build a mobile tool that tells frontline health workers which households to screen first for tuberculosis and other infections.
The grant comes with $200,000 in Google Cloud credits and pro bono engineering support. It is Google.org’s second grant to the company, after funding a validation study of its AI-NETRA platform in 2025.
How the Company Was Selected
Froncort.AI is one of 15 organisations worldwide picked for the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, a $30 million programme whose recipients were announced on 15 September.
Read More: Sachin Tendulkar Backs Waste Management Startup Recykal
Funding Confido Health Raises $12.5 Million To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI Funding Prodoc AI Raises Seed Funding From Dr A. Velumani Family Office
Google.org said winners were chosen from more than 2,600 proposals. Froncort.AI is one of four recipients in the health category, alongside Flexbone, Helium Health Foundation and the University of Warwick.
Read More: How to Choose the Best Travel Agency in Jaipur for a Memorable Rajasthan Holiday
That ratio explains why the grant matters more than its size. Being selected from 2,600 applicants is third-party validation that a health ministry or a state programme can cite.
What mAI-NETRA Does
The grant funds mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of the company’s public health platform.
Froncort.AI’s system combines government health programme data with satellite-derived insights from Google’s Earth AI models. It also weighs local indicators such as settlement density, land use, rainfall and flood exposure.
From that, it flags higher-risk areas within 300-metre zones and turns them into ranked work plans, household clusters and routes that health workers can follow on field visits.
The Froncort.AI app works offline with automatic sync and offers multilingual voice guidance. Matters in districts where connectivity is patchy.
Why Routing Beats Testing Alone
India’s tuberculosis programme already has tests, drugs and reporting systems. What it lacks is a way to decide where to spend a health worker’s day.
Sending a worker street by street in a high-burden district is expensive and random. Sending the same worker to a ranked cluster of households with recent flooding and dense housing is a different use of the same salary.
Froncort.AI already has TB and malaria modules are already in place. The platform is being built to cover six diseases: TB, leprosy, malaria, dengue, cholera and leptospirosis.
What the Founder Says
“The world does not lack experts. It lacks their reach,” said Ujjwal Rao, founder and chief executive of Froncort.AI. He described AI-NETRA as putting that expertise in the health worker’s hands at the door, showing where to go, whom to screen and when.
India’s health system already collects enormous amounts of data through national programmes. The gap is turning that data into a route a health worker can follow on a Tuesday morning.

AI video production startup Lemonpeel raises $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by Shastra VC
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Sta
Gyan Vardhan
17 Nov 2026
14:09
IST
Follow Us
New Update
AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.
The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.
Co-founded in Sep. last year by Hardik Goyal, Riddhiman Pal and Abhinav Nikam, Lemonpeel builds AI video production infrastructure for enterprise creative teams that brings together video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery through specialised agents and a model-agnostic engine. It works with customers in India and the UAE.
The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products.
The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities.
Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.
Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels.
Meanwhile, Clueso raised $10 million in a Series A round in Oct. this year, led by Dharana Capital, to strengthen its AI agents and automate enterprise video creation and editing workflows.
TrueFan AI also secured $10 million in Series A funding in June this year, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners, to scale its enterprise video-generation infrastructure. Other emerging players include CRAON, which raised pre-seed funding in May 2026 to develop its prompt-led AI video editing platform.

articles.text:
Snippets
AI infra startup JohnAIC raises $1.9 Mn in pre-seed round
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
Shashank Pathak
17 Nov 2026
09:38
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
The proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing, configuration and supply capabilities for AI servers. It aims to scale production capacity to up to 100 AI servers per month.
Founded by Sasank Chilamkurthy, JohnAIC builds on-premise AI infrastructure combining GPU servers, inference software, optimised open-source models and local data management. Its integrated systems are designed to help enterprises deploy AI within their own environments while retaining control over computing resources, models and data.
The startup serves public sector organisations and large enterprises, including banks, healthcare companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs). For BFSI institutions, its systems enable AI deployment behind organisational firewalls and are designed to support DPDP and RBI requirements.
JohnAIC is also working with Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL). Its server infrastructure has been deployed for routine operational surveys, converting field data into real-time insights.
The company is expanding its factory and supply chain infrastructure to address demand from Indian enterprises building private AI environments and neocloud infrastructure.
